findings.title: A global view grant also grants global group management
findings.body: The all-groups check for `canManage()` accepts both `VIEW` and `MANAGE`. As a result, an administrator granted only `VIEW` on the all-groups resource is treated as able to manage groups; for example, `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` relies on this no-argument check and will let that administrator create groups. Restrict this check to the `MANAGE` scope.

findings.title: Group view permissions are collected using authorization resource IDs
findings.body: `hasPermission` expects a group ID and looks up the resource by its name, but this passes the authorization resource's ID. It therefore fails to evaluate the matching per-group resource and may fall back to the all-groups resource instead. Line 123 also adds that authorization resource ID to the result, although callers use this set to filter users by their actual group IDs. Group-scoped user searches and counts consequently omit users with only per-group member-view permissions.
